pr.title: offset_of: allow (unstably) taking the offset of slice tail fields
pr.description:
Fields of type `[T]` have a statically known offset, so there is no reason to forbid them in `offset_of!`. This PR adds the `offset_of_slice` feature to allow them.

I created a tracking issue: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/126151.
pr.author: RalfJung

processing.reason: This PR is a feature-enabling change, not a value-changing miscompilation. The old `TyAndLayout::offset_of_subfield` helper did not compute a different offset for slice-tail fields; it hit an `assert!(layout.is_sized(), "offset of unsized field ... cannot be computed statically")` and aborted/panicked. The old type checker likewise rejected such fields with E0277 unless the new `offset_of_slice` feature was enabled. The corrected code computes the same offsets but permits a slice tail because it has static alignment. Therefore there is no source-grounded original-vs-transformed pair of successfully executing functions that produce differing concrete values: the historical behavior is a compile-time rejection/assertion, not a wrong runtime result. Encoding that as a sentinel value or runtime panic would be an arbitrary return-value change unsupported by the PR.

analysis.summary: Feature PR (not a confirmed regression fix): the three const-folding passes must evaluate `NullOp::OffsetOf` through the current `ParamEnv` and permit an unsized slice tail whose offset is statically known. The old shared helper asserted every offset subfield was sized; the replacement computes offsets to a slice tail and only rejects other unsized tails.
analysis.originalLogic: The old `TyAndLayout::offset_of_subfield` helper accumulated variant/field offsets and required every intermediate field layout to be sized: it contained `assert!(` followed by `layout.is_sized(),` and the message `"offset of unsized field (type {:?}) cannot be computed statically"`. In `DataflowConstProp`, `GVN`, and `KnownPanicsLint`, `NullOp::OffsetOf` was folded with that helper, e.g. `layout.offset_of_subfield(&self.ecx, fields.iter()).bytes()` / `op_layout.offset_of_subfield(self, fields.iter()).bytes()`. Type checking likewise used `self.require_type_is_sized(field_ty, expr.span, ObligationCauseCode::Misc);` for offset fields.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior for the new input domain was to treat every unsized `offset_of!` subfield as statically uncomputable. The old assertion says `"offset of unsized field (type {:?}) cannot be computed statically"`, but the PR states: `"Fields of type `[T]` have a statically known offset, so there is no reason to forbid them in `offset_of!`."` The corrected logic permits a non-sized layout only when its tail is a slice: `if !layout.is_sized() {` ... `let tail = self.struct_tail_erasing_lifetimes(layout.ty, param_env);` ... `if !matches!(tail.kind(), ty::Slice(..)) {` then it reports a compiler bug with `"offset of not-statically-aligned field (type {:?}) cannot be computed statically"`. This is feature-enabling pass correctness, not evidence of a reproduced miscompilation.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR containing `NullOp::OffsetOf` produced by `std::mem::offset_of!` on `#[repr(C)]` structs whose final field is a slice `[i32]`, including nested struct and tuple-tail cases. The PR's run-pass inputs are `struct S { a: u8, b: (u8, u8), c: [i32] }`, `struct T { x: i8, y: S }`, and `type Tup = (i16, [i32]);`, compiled with `#![feature(offset_of_slice, offset_of_nested)]`. Negative inputs include the same fields without the feature and tuples with a non-tail unsized element.
analysis.trigger: A `NullOp::OffsetOf` is being const-folded in DataflowConstProp, GVN, or KnownPanicsLint for a field layout that is not sized because the field type ends in a slice tail `[T]`, under the `offset_of_slice` feature. Type checking also reaches this case when `offset_of!` names a slice-tailed field without requiring full `Sized`.
preconditions: The source uses `std::mem::offset_of!` and, for slice-tail fields, enables `#![feature(offset_of_slice)]`; nested field syntax also requires `offset_of_nested`.

The unsized field is a slice tail (`[T]`), not an arbitrary unsized type such as a trait object; type checking uses `require_type_has_static_alignment` and only exempts `trivially_sized` or `ty::Slice` tails.

The offset expression must be evaluated with the function/const-eval `ParamEnv`, not a context-free layout helper: new code uses `self.ecx.tcx.offset_of_subfield(self.ecx.param_env(), layout, fields.iter())` or equivalent.
For a tuple, only the last element may have a dynamically sized type, as exercised by `offset_of!(([u8], u8), 1)` being rejected.
pitfalls: Do not generalize slice-tail support to every unsized field: the new helper still calls `bug!("offset of not-statically-aligned field (type {:?}) cannot be computed statically", layout.ty)` when a non-sized tail is not `ty::Slice(..)`.
Do not evaluate `OffsetOf` without `ParamEnv`; all three pass changes switch from the layout-only helper to `TyCtxt::offset_of_subfield(param_env, layout, indices)`.
Do not weaken the feature gate: without `offset_of_slice`, the expected diagnostics are `E0277` such as `the size for values of type `[i32]` cannot be known at compilation time`.
An old test name or retained `require_type_is_sized` call does not mean the slice-tail case should still be rejected; check the actual value assignments and feature-gated branch.
`offset_of!(T, y)` where `T` itself has a slice tail is valid under the feature, and `offset_of!(T, y.c)` additionally needs the nested-field feature.
analysis.testStrategy: Use focused compile/run UI tests. Positive case: with `#![feature(offset_of_slice, offset_of_nested)]`, a `#[repr(C)]` struct ending in `[i32]`, a wrapper struct, and a tuple ending in `[i32]` should have statically folded offsets; the PR's expectations are `offset_of!(S, c) == 4`, `offset_of!(T, y) == 4`, `offset_of!(T, y.c) == 8`, and `offset_of!(Tup, 1) == 4`. Negative case: the same slice-tail fields without the feature must still fail with `E0277`; `offset_of!(([u8], u8), 1)` must fail because only a tuple's last element may be unsized. For pass-specific coverage, inspect MIR before/after DataflowConstProp, GVN, and KnownPanicsLint to confirm `OffsetOf` is folded to the same scalar for slice-tail inputs and that no sized-field assertion fires. No compiler build or execution was performed for this analysis.
